chapter: Leading the band after Chick Webb, 1939-40
title: Coleman Hawkins's horn, and Lonnie Simmons joins
summary: Elmer kept Hawkins's tenor and McRae bought him another; Lonnie Simmons then played the Famous Door, Roseland and Apollo.

bands.name: Ella Fitzgerald and Her Famous Orchestra

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Yeah. And Coleman Hawkins was standing over on the side. He said, 'Where you been?' He told Elmer, 'I thought you was coming back, you know, after the theater. You was going to bring my horn back' -- I didn't know Elmer had his horn all the time. Elmer took the horn to the coast. Because we used to laugh. We sat up there and laughed like mad. Elmer had Coleman Hawkins -- I say, 'I don't blame him. I wouldn't give it back to you either.' I say, 'That horn you

got, that's a beautiful" -- He say, "You got one. Why you didn't lend him your horn?" I say, "Well it's not here. I don't take but one on the road. We was laughing. We made a big joke out of it. So the next day I went down to the music store and bought Elmer a horn, you know, and we came on back here. But Elmer Williams left us right after that night. And when we came back -- I think that's when I put this boy -- MR. WELBURN: Lonnie Simmons. MR. MC RAE: Lonnie Simmons. I think I put Lonnie in. Elmer didn't -- I know we got Elmer a horn, but Lonnie must've joined us in Chicago. Because I know Elmer didn't leave Chicago with us. But I know I did -- I know it was a horn. Moe Gale say, "What was this horn business about?" I say, "Well I had to buy Elmer a horn."

He had another date or so to play with Lonnie Simmonds. us. So when Lonnie was there, we got (inaudible).
Lonnie played the Famous Door with us, the Roseland, and the Apollo Theater. And that the four weeks before we went back to the hotel in Boston.
Now if you ask me about that hotel in Boston, I don't know because we had played that hotel once before with Chick.
